mechanism_narrative: Rising RSAFS (retail sales) signals robust consumer spending, directly supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS rises by >0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy, compressing equity valuations via higher discount rates and reducing liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous UNRATE increase (>0.1pp) and INDPRO decrease (<109.5) indicate labor market deterioration and production slowdown, triggering negative equity returns through earnings contraction over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.1pp and INDPRO falls < 109.5 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.1pp and INDPRO falls < 109.5.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDP growth >3% and UNRATE <5%), rising HOUST signals sustained consumer confidence and housing demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: Rising INDPRO (industrial production) reflects expanding manufacturing output, directly correlating with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO rises by >0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE above 5.0% indicates labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending power and corporate revenue, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL rise (>0.5%) with stable FEDFUNDS (<4.5%) signals inflation without policy response, increasing equity volatility and causing negative returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 4.5%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL >200), S&P 500 returns turn negative over 60 days due to reduced economic activity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances during monetary tightening cycles.
